previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a thrombosed left upper extremity AV graft, which prevented dialysis access. She underwent surgical exploration, but the procedure was aborted due to inadequate arterial inflow, making revision unfeasible. The graft was deemed non-salvageable, and hemodialysis was resumed using a tunneled catheter in the left internal jugular vein, requiring TPA to restore function. The patient tolerated dialysis with episodes of hypotension, and her incision healed without complications. Medication adjustments were made for nausea and hypotension, switching from long-acting to short-acting nitrates. A transvaginal ultrasound revealed a thickened endometrium and calcified fibroids, prompting planned gynecologic follow-up. She was discharged to a 30-day respite care facility with ongoing outpatient dialysis and scheduled appointments for vascular access and gynecologic evaluation.

Brief Hospital Course:

ACTIVE ISSUES BY PROBLEM:
# Calciphylaxis: Patient presented with two painful indurated 
lesions over inner thigh and left hip that were consistent with 
calciphylaxis on punch biopsy. CT scan identified some 
calcifications and no signs of infection. Patient was started on 
sodium thiosulfate on ___ and dialysis frequency was increased 
to daily for one week. Calcium-phos product was kept below 55. 
She had significant nausea with sodium thiosulfate but was 
willing to continue 3x/weekly treatments. She will also require 
4x/weekly dialysis until follow-up with her outpatient 
nephrologist. Her pain was controlled with oxycontin and 
dilaudid. She should be seen by dermatology next week to monitor 
her thigh and hip lesions.

# Chronic pannus wound: 
Has a persistent, slow to heal pannus wound followed by 
transplant surgery as an outpatient. Wound care was consulted 
for management of abdominal wound and felt it was healing well. 
She will continue to follow with transplant surgery after 
discharge.

# Urinary tract infection:  
Grossly positive UA with frank pyuria and complaints of dysuria, 
all consistent with likely infection.  Given cefepime in the ER, 
which was transitioned to cipro given her past urine cultures 
have grown bacteria all susceptible to cipro.  She will need a 
14 day course given this qualifies as a complicated UTI 
(___).

# Nausea, vomiting: 
___ have been due to UTI (see below) vs reaction to her calcium 
acetate (as this gives her nausea when she takes it). Later 
developed nausea with sodium thiosulfate therapy. LFTs within 
normal limits, troponin elevated but flat and MB negative so do 
not suspect cardiac ischemia. Benign abdomen (other than pain 
over wound site) was reassuring for intra-abdominal cause. Her 
symptoms were managed with ativan, zofran, and reglan.

# Chest pain, CAD s/p CABG: History initially concerning for 
NSTEMI vs. unstable angina but initial changes on EKG appeared 
to be due only to lead placement, and cardiac enzymes showed 
mildly elevated troponin that remained stable (and is consistent 
with past baseline) and negative MB.  She was continued on home 
regimen of metoprolol, atorvastatin, plavix, and isosorbide 
dinitrate.  No aspirin given due to allergy.

# HTN: Poorly controlled despite frequent dialysis. Patient had 
no symptoms of hypertensive urgency. Her regimen was uptitrated 
over the course of her stay and she was discharged on isosorbide 
dinitrite 30mg three times a day and 5mg amlodipine daily. This 
will likely need to be uptitrated further.

INACTIVE ISSUES BY PROBLEM:
# ESRD: continued on HD, initially MWF then daily once diagnosis 
of calciphylaxis was made, now with plans to transition to 
4x/weekly. Calcium acetate was changed to lanthanum for phos 
binder given her nausea with calcium acetate.

radiology_notes.text:
CT EXAMINATION OF THE PELVIS AND BILATERAL LOWER EXTREMITIES WITHOUT
INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST

CLINICAL INDICATION:  ___ female with end-stage renal disease and
chronic non-healing abdominal pannus wound and new areas of hyperpigmentation,
evaluate for calciphylaxis.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT imaging of the pelvis and bilateral lower
extremities to the level of the knee joints was performed without the use of
intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformatted images were also
obtained.

COMPARISON:  CT pelvis dated ___.

FINDINGS:

No acute fracture is identified within the visualized osseous structures. 
There is moderate degenerative change of the sacroiliac joints with
subchondral sclerosis and vacuum phenomenon (6:19).  Mild degenerative change
is present about the bilateral femoroacetabular joints with joint space loss
and spurring.  There is evidence of right total knee arthroplasty without
hardware complication.  No osseous destructive lesions are seen.

There are multiple subcutaneous nodules within the anterior abdominal wall
measuring up to 1.3 cm (4:28).  There is redemonstration of a soft tissue
defect along the left lower abdomen consistent with the patient's wound
(4:41).  This wound does not extend to the abdominal wall musculature.  There
are also multiple subcutaneous nodules along the medial aspect of the left
thigh which demonstrate peripheral rim calcification measuring up to 2.3 x 1.2
cm (4:125).

There are dense vascular calcifications throughout all the visualized
vasculature extending from the abdominal aorta to the popliteal vessels
bilaterally.

There is a fat-containing umbilical hernia (4:13).  Multiple calcified
fibroids are present within the pelvis.  There is colonic diverticulosis
without evidence of acute diverticulitis.  No free fluid is seen.  There is no
inguinal lymphadenopathy present.

There is mild atrophic change within the medial gastrocnemius musculature
bilaterally.  The remainder of the visualized musculature is grossly
preserved.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Dense vascular calcifications, as well as multiple subcutaneous nodules
within the anterior abdominal wall in the left medial thigh.

2.  Multiple calcified uterine fibroids.

3.  Colonic diverticulosis without evidence of acute diverticulitis.

4.  Soft tissue defect within the left lower abdomen consistent with the
patient's clinical non-healing wound that does not extend to the left
abdominal musculature.

5.  Moderate degenerative change within the sacroiliac joints bilaterally.
